chunks: From him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):
Regarding a man who gives charity (sadaqah), is it permissible for him to inherit it? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the Two (Imams), a common honorific referring to Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them).
key_terms.صَدَقَة: Charity, a voluntary gift given for the sake of God, often implying a transfer of ownership.
key_terms.يَرِثَهَا: To inherit it, referring to receiving the property as an heir.

ai.seo_question: Can a person inherit property they previously gave as charity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence: donating a specific item as *sadaqah* does not necessarily sever the donor's right to inherit it, provided the donation was not conditional upon relinquishing inheritance rights. This ruling distinguishes between general charitable giving and specific bequests, emphasizing that ownership transfer for charity purposes does not automatically exclude the donor from the legal framework of inheritance (*mirath*).
